series.label: unassigned mark near the origin (Dr .30 or Dr .48 group)

FC-5A.notes_for_reviewers: Failure envelopes of SS soil (white silica sand): maximum shear stress against normal stress, in psf, for four density groups. Dr is relative density. Legend: open circles Dr .02 to .13 (the 29 degree line), squares Dr .30 (32.8 degrees), triangles pointing down Dr .48 (36.9 degrees), triangles pointing up Dr .77 (41.5 degrees). Each straight line is the authors' fit through its group's symbols; several lines are drawn with gaps, and a crosshair in a white gap is a no. Near the origin all four lines meet and symbols overlap: answer cannot tell where the shape cannot be seen. One row asks about a possible symbol hidden in the merged lines near sigma 300, tau 240 psf (the row names an unassigned mark): in A say whether a symbol center is in the box at all, in B write cannot tell unless the shape is clear, and name the shape in C if it is.

FC-6A.title: Figure C-6A: Failure Envelopes - Maximum Shear Stress vs. Normal Stress (printed C-17, PDF 131)
FC-6A.legend_hint: see the notes on this figure
FC-6A.notes_for_reviewers: Failure envelopes of LSM soil (a mixture of crushed scoria and air-floated clay): maximum shear stress against normal stress, in psf, for three density groups (Dr is relative density). Legend: triangles Dr .05 to .40, open circles Dr .19 to .28, squares Dr 1.03 to 1.07. The three lines carry no labels and run close together. At the right end the triangles' line is the highest, the circles' line is in the middle and the squares' line is the lowest. The circles' and the squares' lines are dashed below about 750 psf of normal stress; the triangles' line is solid down to the origin. The thin dashed lines marked 3820 and 3680 are construction lines, not data. One circle is printed outside the frame, below and left of the origin, on the dashed end of the circles' line; it is a real printed circle. A crosshair in the white gap of a dashed line is a no.

FC-7A.title: Figure C-7A: Failure Envelopes - Maximum Shear Stress vs. Normal Shear Stress (printed C-21, PDF 135)
FC-7A.legend_hint: see the notes on this figure
FC-7A.notes_for_reviewers: Failure envelopes of RSM-b soil (a mixture of crushed scoria and crushed marble): shear load against normal load, both in psi, for two density groups (Dr is relative density). Legend: circles with a dot in the center, Dr 0.53 (the 45 degree line); triangles with a dot inside, Dr 1.0 (the 50.5 degree line). Each line is solid through the symbols and continues as a dashed line to the shear axis at the left; a crosshair in a white gap of the dashed part is a no.
